reason: Rolling Core releases: serve adopts an inherited listening socket (LISTEN_FDS or --listen-fd) and probes with SO_REUSEADDR; a stopping supervisor generation drains relayed requests for at most 5 s while deployment operations run shielded and are joined before host authority is released; execution workers resend read-only host observations only when the host provably did not dispatch them (connect failure or the new undispatched 503 marker); the handoff inventory keeps a project finishing while a queued follow-up dispatch is in flight. Selected suites cover the handoff agent contract, listener adoption and the restart probe, the management ledger under request cancellation, IPC client/server, host-service replacement and resend bounds, supervisor lifecycle and bootstrap, and the browser bridge that now rides the resending client.
exclusions: test_runtime_host_services.py is selected per test: its product-guidance mirror cases and the API-peer 401/404 case fail identically on clean main (pre-existing) and are excluded. Process-level suites need a pidfd-capable Python with Nebula importable by spawned workers; locally they were run with Python 3.12 on SQLite and PostgreSQL. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed; browser reconnect across a host swap is recorded as unverified. scripts/deploy_rehearsal and the docs are rehearsal tooling and evidence, exercised on a scratch Core (E4-E6 in docs/validation/rolling-core-releases.md), not by CI.
